202A.11 / CHAPTER 11 OF 11

How to trade the demand wave

How big could the wave be, when could it arrive, and which approach can capture it?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Price moves at the margin02Liquidity & price impact03Buy/sell pressure04Supply transfer05Early wallet flow06Demand acceleration07Attention conversion08Push, Hold or Fail09Meta saturation10Three basic checks11How to trade the demand wave

01Definition

Assess the coming flow of demand first, then shape the trade around its expected size and timing. Snipe and swing are containers for capturing an early entry and selling into the rise; PvP adds competition for the same attention and capital.

02Why it matters

You enter early, before the expected rise, and sell into that rise. A good story at a late price is a different opportunity. The approach must fit the demand wave rather than forcing the token into a preferred holding period.

03What to check

  • Assess the wave: use the three basic checks to identify fresh demand, plausible scale, timing and competing tokens. Use 202B.10 if the expected wave needs a swing window.
  • Shape the container: choose snipe, PvP rotation, or swing; define an early entry condition, exposure that fits usable liquidity, and where or when to sell into the expected rise.
  • Define the frame: state the required upward pressure, the time allowed for it to produce the move, and the exit when it fails, fades, or the planned rise has been captured.

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

Entry precedes the anticipated run. Demand and price follow-through develop inside the defined window, and exits realize gains into the rise. Exposure fits executable liquidity.

Dangerous

Entry chases a wave that has already passed. The required buying fails to arrive, sellers take over, or a failed snipe is relabeled as a swing to avoid exiting.

05Beginner mistake

Choosing the holding period first, treating a later recovery as proof that a failed snipe worked, or waiting indefinitely for a thesis to become demand.

06Takeaway

Assess the wave, build the container, enter early, and sell into the rise. If the necessary pressure fails within the defined frame and time, the trade has failed.

Assess demand → choose the container → enter early → sell into the rise → exit on failure.

Snipe: upward pressure must exist immediately or be building, and produce the run while you are in. Without it, within this snipe frame the trade can only go down: exit.

Frame and time define success. A later recovery outside the window cannot validate the original snipe.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    Snipe entry: assume the basic checks pass. At minute 0, price is 1.00, fresh buyers are arriving and dips recover. The planned wave is 1.20-1.30 within five minutes. Enter only near 1.00-1.05 while that early condition holds; a first look at 1.25 is already outside this entry plan.

  2. 02

    Capture the run: at minute 2, buying drives price to 1.22. The plan sells half in 1.20-1.25 and exits the rest by 1.30, on fading pressure, or at minute 5, whichever comes first. Order size must fit current buy and sell quotes.

  3. 03

    Failure: exit earlier if the 1.00 area fails without recovery or buying stops advancing price. If no sustained move above 1.05 occurs by minute 3, exit rather than wait for minute 5. A later rally cannot validate this failed snipe.

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

Illustrative snipe: the basic checks pass and at minute 0 price is 1.00 with fresh buyers and recovering dips. The entry region is 1.00-1.05; the expected run is 1.20-1.30 within five minutes. At minute 2, price reaches 1.22 and the plan sells half. Exit the rest by 1.30, on fading buying, or at minute 5, whichever comes first. Exit earlier if the 1.00 area fails without recovery or price cannot sustain above 1.05 by minute 3. For a PvP variation, a rival gains fresh buyers while this token loses pressure: reassess the original trade and run fresh checks before any rotation, without extending its deadline. These are invented numbers for teaching the plan.

How to investigate it

Write demand source, expected size and arrival window first. Record an entry region, position size against current buy and sell quotes, profit-taking into the rise, follow-through deadline and earlier invalidation. Keep the same plan while assessing pressure. In PvP, compare rivals over the same windows; attention rotating away can end the chosen wave. If the expected demand needs days, move to 202B.10 and 202B.11 before entry. A five-minute collection cannot resolve the minute-by-minute example; execution requires fresher evidence.

Check your reasoning — answered

Price stays at 1.02 through minute 3, then reaches 1.25 at minute 8. Did the planned snipe succeed? No. The required sustained move above 1.05 failed by minute 3, so the plan called for exit. Minute 8 is outside the frame; it is a new opportunity to assess.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Snipe

Compare sampled buying, selling, absorption, and price response in Inspect; use Tweet for competing story evidence and Swing for longer-horizon leads. The scheduled sample cannot establish immediate execution timing or a complete live tape.

Go deeper

The example uses invented price units and a five-minute window to demonstrate a complete plan; these are not universal thresholds. Snipe upward pressure must be immediate or building and produce price follow-through during the intended exposure. Set the deadline before entry. No follow-through or fading pressure means exit, not conversion to a swing. PvP adds competition for the same participation: compare rival attention, fresh buyers, remaining inventory and usable liquidity. Reassess current leadership without chasing a rival whose wave has already run. Snipe timing can overlap with PvP; the first token need not fail before capital rotates. Migration may create anticipation, but completion alone does not create new buying. When the expected wave builds over days, use the comprehensive assessment in 202B.10 and execution in 202B.11. The low and high are planned entry and exit regions, not exact extrema known in advance.
